AuthzType.description:
Which [`crate::authorizer::Authorizer`] impl to instantiate.
`snake_case` to match the spec's `type = "allow_all" | "simple" |
"opa"` wire shape.

`allow_all` is the default and is not an authorizer: it allows every
principal every operation, and the ACL administration RPCs answer
`SECURITY_DISABLED` (54),
as Kafka does with no `authorizer.class.name`. `simple` and `opa` are
decision
points, and under either the ACL RPCs serve requests normally.

BackgroundUncleanRecovery.description:
What the background unclean-recovery path does when it cannot ask anybody
for a break-glass approval.

The controller starts unclean recovery from leader election and from the
broker-heartbeat path. Neither carries a request context, so neither has a
caller to refuse. An operator who types an unclean election can be asked
for a second signature; a controller that reacts to a dead broker at 03:00
cannot.

The TOML spelling is `off | audit-only | require`, so the serde rename is
`kebab-case`.

oneOf.description: Recovery runs and writes no break-glass audit event.

Recovery runs and writes a bypassed break-glass audit event naming the
partition and the strategy. An operator can then prove after the fact
that a data-losing election happened with no approval.

Recovery does not run. The partition stays leaderless and visibly
offline, and the refusal is audited.

every_n.description: Emit a checkpoint after this many audit records.

every_secs.description: Emit a checkpoint at least this often, in seconds.

checkpoint.description:
Checkpoint emission cadence. An absent table keeps the current
cadence, which starts at the defaults.

enabled.description: Whether the audit subsystem is active.

failure_mode.description: Whether privileged operations continue when audit processing fails.

signing.description:
Ed25519 checkpoint signing key. An absent table keeps the current key.
The broker has none by default: chaining only, no checkpoints.

spool.description:
Durable spool for the AU-5 degraded path. An absent table keeps the
current spool settings, which start at the defaults.

topic.description:
Internal topic name for audit records. It has to start with `__`: the
broker reports it internal on `Metadata` and refuses to freeze it by
that prefix, and a name outside the convention would satisfy only the
first of the two.

key_id.description:
Key id recorded on each checkpoint, so a verifier can follow a key
rotation.

key_path.description: Path to the PKCS#8 Ed25519 private key that signs audit checkpoints.

FileAuditSpoolConfig.description: `[audit.spool]` — durable spool for the AU-5 degraded path.

dir.description:
Directory that holds the spool files. A relative path resolves under
the broker's log directory.

max_bytes.description: Cap on the total size of the spool on disk.

sync_every_n.description: Number of appended records between durable file syncs.

FileAuthorizationConfig.description:
TOML shape of `[authorization]`. `type` (renamed to `authz_type` on
the Rust side to avoid shadowing the keyword) defaults to
`AllowAll`; `super_users` is the principal bypass list consulted by
every concrete authorizer impl.

Omitting the whole block leaves the cluster with no authorizer, which is
what Kafka has when `authorizer.class.name` is unset: every principal is
allowed everything, and the ACL administration RPCs -- `DescribeAcls`,
`CreateAcls` and `DeleteAcls` -- answer `SECURITY_DISABLED` (54) rather
than an empty listing or a stored binding nothing would consult.
`kafka-acls` reports that refusal.

`deny_unknown_fields` so a misspelled `super_user` typo at the top
of the `[authorization]` block is rejected at parse time rather
than silently producing the wrong authorizer.

allow_everyone_if_no_acl_found.description:
Kafka's `allow.everyone.if.no.acl.found`. Only consulted by
`type = "simple"`. When `true`, a request is allowed if NO ACL at all
applies to the resource -- by type, name, and LITERAL/PREFIXED/wildcard
pattern, regardless of principal, host, operation, or permission type.
If at least one ACL applies to the resource and none of them matches,
the request is still denied. Default `false`, matching Kafka's
`StandardAuthorizer`.

opa.description:
`Some` iff `authz_type == Opa`. Required in that case;
`apply_to` returns
[`FileConfigError::MissingSection`][crate::file_config::FileConfigError::MissingSection]
when omitted.

super_users.description:
Principals that bypass every ACL check, Kafka's `super.users`. The
active authorizer and the delegation-token `act-as` gate both read it.
An entry may use Kafka's `User:<name>` form. `User:ANONYMOUS` is
accepted, as in Kafka. Empty is the default and grants no bypass.

FileBreakGlassConfig.description:
TOML shape of `[break_glass]`. Maps to
[`crate::config::BreakGlassConfig`].

Every field is `Option`, so `approvers = []` and `signed_actions = []` are
each a written choice and are distinct from omitting the key.
`deny_unknown_fields` so a misspelled key is rejected at parse time.

approvers.description:
Principals that may approve a proposal. Omitted leaves the
`BrokerConfig` value, which is empty.

background_unclean_recovery.description:
What the background unclean-recovery path does, where there is no
caller to ask for an approval. Default
[`BackgroundUncleanRecovery::AuditOnly`].

proposal_ttl.description:
How long a proposal stays usable. Default
[`crate::config::DEFAULT_BREAK_GLASS_PROPOSAL_TTL`].

required_approvals.description:
Distinct approving principals a proposal needs. Default
[`crate::config::DEFAULT_BREAK_GLASS_REQUIRED_APPROVALS`]. Values below
[`crate::config::MIN_BREAK_GLASS_REQUIRED_APPROVALS`] are a startup
error: a two-person rule with one approval is one person.

signed_actions.description:
Actions whose approvals must also carry a detached operator signature.
Omitted inside a present `[break_glass]` section selects
[`crate::config::DEFAULT_BREAK_GLASS_SIGNED_ACTIONS`], the irreversible
set. Naming any action with no `[[operator_keys]]` entry is a startup
error; write `signed_actions = []` to demand no signature.

FileClientAuthMode.description:
Whether a TLS listener asks for and requires a client certificate,
Kafka's `ssl.client.auth`. `Disabled` is the default and never asks;
`Optional` asks and accepts a connection that presents none; `Required`
rejects a connection that presents none. `Optional` and `Required` both
need a `client_ca_path`.

FileDelegationTokenConfig.description:
TOML shape of `[delegation_token]`. Maps to the three `delegation_token_*`
fields on [`crate::BrokerConfig`].

default_renew_period_ms.description:
Default renew period — the initial `expiry_timestamp_ms` offset
at create time and the implicit renew period when
`RenewDelegationToken.renew_period_ms == -1`. Distinct from
`max_lifetime_ms` (the absolute ceiling). Default 24 hours.

expiry_check_interval_ms.description: Background sweep cadence, ms. Default 1 hour.

max_lifetime_ms.description: Hard upper bound on token lifetime, ms. Default 7 days.

secret_key.description:
HMAC master key. Overridden by `KRABKA_DELEGATION_TOKEN_SECRET_KEY`
when set. Bytes are wrapped in
[`krabka_security::SecretBytes`] before reaching `BrokerConfig`.

FileFreezeConfig.description:
TOML shape of `[freeze]`. Maps to [`crate::config::FreezeConfig`].

Every field is `Option`: a present value replaces the current broker value,
an absent one retains it. `deny_unknown_fields` so a misspelled
`require_signature` is rejected at parse time rather than leaving the
broker on the opposite policy to the one the operator wrote.

max_entries.description:
Ceiling on live freeze registry entries. Default
[`crate::config::DEFAULT_FREEZE_MAX_ENTRIES`]. Must be at least 1.

require_signature.description:
**Security-sensitive.** Demand a detached operator signature on a
freeze as well as on a thaw. Default `false`, which keeps a freeze
available in one command during an incident on a cluster with no key
material yet. A thaw is signed either way.

Setting this to `true` with no `[[operator_keys]]` entry is a startup
error: there would be no key to verify the demanded signature against.

signature_max_skew.description:
How far a signed freeze record's timestamp may sit from the
controller's clock. Default
[`crate::config::DEFAULT_FREEZE_SIGNATURE_MAX_SKEW`].

FileGssapiConfig.description:
TOML shape of `[gssapi]`. Maps to
[`crate::network::auth::GssapiConfig`]. `principal_to_local_rules`
are parsed into `KerberosRule` at `apply_to` time.

kdc.description:
KDC endpoint (e.g. `tcp://kdc:88`) that bypasses krb5.conf discovery;
falls back to krb5.conf when omitted.

keytab_path.description:
Keytab that holds this broker's Kerberos service key. The SASL/GSSAPI
accept path reads it to answer a client's ticket.

max_time_skew.description: Maximum tolerated difference between client and broker clocks.

principal_to_local_rules.description:
`auth_to_local` rule specs, applied in order (first match wins). Kafka's
default for `sasl.kerberos.principal.to.local.rules` is `["DEFAULT"]`,
and an empty list maps no principal.

realm.description:
Default Kerberos realm, the only realm the `DEFAULT` rule accepts.
Kafka reads it from `krb5.conf`; when it is omitted `DEFAULT` matches
no principal and the rules have to name the realm.

FileInterBrokerCredentials.description:
TOML shape of `[inter_broker_credentials]`. A `type` discriminator
selects the variant. PLAIN/SCRAM inter-broker over TOML remain
intentionally unexposed.

client_principal.description:
Kerberos principal this broker authenticates as when it dials a
peer.

kdc_url.description:
KDC endpoint (for example `tcp://kdc:88`) used to obtain the
service ticket, bypassing krb5.conf discovery.

keytab_path.description: Keytab that holds the key for `client_principal`.

service_name.description:
The peer's `sasl.kerberos.service.name`. Defaults to `"kafka"`
when omitted.

token_path.description:
File containing the bearer token. A trailing newline is ignored.
The token itself never appears in the parsed config's `Debug` form.

bootstrap.description:
`host:port` the manager dials to reach its own broker.
May be empty; the broker derives the address from the inter-broker
listener at startup.

event_queue_capacity.description: Capacity of the shared metadata-event delivery queue.

fetch_max_bytes.description: Maximum bytes returned by each per-partition metadata fetch.

fetch_max_wait.description: Maximum wait for each per-partition metadata fetch.

fetch_retry_backoff.description: Backoff after a failed metadata fetch.

in_memory.description:
Explicit opt-out: run the non-durable in-memory RLMM instead of the
topic-backed default. Tests / single-node dev only.

min_isr.description:
`min.insync.replicas` for `__remote_log_metadata` on first creation.
Defaults to 2 (Kafka's `remote.log.metadata.topic.min.isr`). Keep it at
or below `replication`: a topic whose `min.insync.replicas` exceeds its
replica count rejects every `acks=all` write, so a single-broker setup
that sets `replication = 1` sets this to 1 as well.

num_partitions.description:
Partition count for `__remote_log_metadata` on first creation.
Defaults to 50 (Kafka's
`remote.log.metadata.topic.num.partitions`).

replication.description:
Replication factor for `__remote_log_metadata` on first
creation. Defaults to 3 (Kafka's
`remote.log.metadata.topic.replication.factor`).

topic_create_timeout.description: Timeout for provisioning each internal metadata topic.

advertised.description:
`host:port` published to clients in `Metadata` responses, Kafka's
`advertised.listeners` entry for this listener.

connections_max_idle.description:
Per-listener `connections.max.idle.ms`. Absent leaves this listener on
the broker-wide `connections_max_idle`. Maps to an entry in
[`crate::BrokerConfig::connections_max_idle_overrides`].

connections_max_reauth.description:
Per-listener KIP-368 `connections.max.reauth.ms`. Absent leaves this
listener on the broker-wide `connections_max_reauth`. Maps to an entry
in [`crate::BrokerConfig::connections_max_reauth_overrides`].

name.description:
Listener name, for example `"PLAINTEXT"` or `"SASL_SSL"`. It is the
name `inter_broker_listener_name` and Kafka's
`listener.security.protocol.map` refer to.

protocol.description:
Security protocol this listener speaks: `Plaintext`, `Ssl`,
`SaslPlaintext`, or `SaslSsl`.

enabled_mechanisms.description:
SASL mechanisms this listener accepts, Kafka's
`sasl.enabled.mechanisms`. Each entry is a wire name such as `PLAIN`,
`SCRAM-SHA-256`, `GSSAPI`, or `OAUTHBEARER`; an unknown name is
rejected at parse time.

FileOAuthBearerConfig.description:
TOML shape of `[oauthbearer]`. Maps to
[`krabka_security::OAuthBearerValidator`]. Setting `jwks_endpoint_uri`
selects the signed-JWT validator; setting
`introspection_endpoint_uri` selects the RFC 7662 introspection
validator; the two endpoint URIs are mutually
exclusive. With neither set, the unsecured-JWS validator
(development only) is used, and that fallback is rejected at
config-load unless `allow_unsecured = true`.

allow_unsecured.description:
Opt-in for the unsecured-JWS (`alg:none`) development
validator. Default false. With neither `jwks_endpoint_uri` nor
`introspection_endpoint_uri` set and a listener enabling
`OAUTHBEARER`, the broker refuses to start rather than silently
trusting unsigned tokens; set this to true to accept that
fallback in development. Never set it in production.

allowable_clock_skew_ms.description:
Clock-skew tolerance, in milliseconds, for `exp` / `iat` / `nbf`.
Default 30000.

custom_claim_check.description:
Optional `JsonPath` expression (RFC 9535, via
jsonpath-rust) evaluated against the token claim set. Token is
rejected when the expression yields empty/null/false. Compiled
once at broker startup; malformed expressions panic with a
descriptive error.

expected_audience.description:
When set, the token `aud` claim must contain this. Signed
validator only.

fallback_user_name_claim.description: Alternate claim name for principal-name fallback.

groups_claim.description:
`JsonPath` expression (RFC 9535) extracting groups.
Compiled once at broker startup; malformed expression panics
with descriptive error.

groups_claim_delimiter.description:
When `groups_claim` resolves to a string, split on
this delimiter.

idp_tls_trust.description:
PEM file containing the CA
certificate(s) used to verify the `IdP`'s TLS certificate on ALL
outbound HTTPS to the `IdP` — JWKS endpoint, introspection
endpoint, and userinfo endpoint. When set, these are
the *only* trust roots used for the outbound HTTPS (replaces the
default webpki-roots — Strimzi-shaped). When unset, the broker
uses reqwest's default rustls webpki-roots.

introspection_client_id.description:
`client_id` the broker uses to authenticate (HTTP Basic
Auth) against the introspection endpoint. Required when
`introspection_endpoint_uri` is set.

introspection_client_secret_path.description:
Filesystem path to a file containing the client
secret the broker uses to authenticate against the introspection
endpoint. Required when `introspection_endpoint_uri` is set.
File-based (not literal) so secret material doesn't sit in the
TOML; operator mounts a `Secret` and writes the mount path here.
The file's trailing newline (if any) is stripped at config-load.

introspection_endpoint_uri.description:
RFC 7662 introspection endpoint URL. When set,
selects the introspection validator (mutually exclusive with
`jwks_endpoint_uri`).

introspection_http_timeout_ms.description:
Timeout for the introspection (and userinfo) HTTP
requests, in milliseconds. Default 10 000 (10 s).

jwks_endpoint_uri.description:
JWKS endpoint URL. When set, tokens are validated as signed
JWTs (RS256 / ES256) against the keys fetched from this URL, and the
broker spawns a background refresher. When unset, the unsecured-JWS
(`alg:none`) development validator is used.

jwks_expiry_seconds.description:
Maximum age (seconds) of the cached JWKS before validators
reject tokens until the next successful refresh. Strimzi default 360
(6 minutes). Unset = no expiry check. Fails
closed on prolonged `IdP` outage. Signed validator only.

jwks_ignore_key_use.description:
When true, the JWKS parser keeps keys regardless of `use`
field. Default false (filter out `use=enc`). Some identity providers
publish signing keys with `use="enc"` by mistake; operators set this
to true to accept them. Signed validator only.

jwks_min_refresh_pause_seconds.description:
Minimum pause (seconds) between on-demand JWKS refreshes
triggered by validator signals (unknown-kid / bad-signature tokens).
Defaults to 1 (Strimzi parity). Signed validator only.

jwks_refresh_interval_ms.description:
JWKS re-fetch interval, in milliseconds. Default 300000
(5 minutes). Signed validator only.

principal_claim_name.description: Claim whose value becomes the principal name. Default `sub`.

userinfo_endpoint_uri.description:
Optional OIDC userinfo endpoint URL. When set, the
introspection validator calls `GET userinfo` after a successful
introspection and merges the profile claims over the
introspection claims (introspection wins for `active`, `exp`,
`iat`, `nbf`, `scope`, `client_id`, `sub`).

valid_issuer_uri.description:
When set, the token `iss` claim must equal this. Signed
validator only.

valid_token_type.description:
Optional JWT `typ` header check. When set, JWT-mode
validators (unsecured + signed JWS) require the JWT header's
`typ` field to equal this string. Introspection-mode skips
(no JWT header). Ignored when unset.

FileOpaConfig.description:
TOML shape of `[authorization.opa]`. Mirrors the constructor
arguments of [`crate::authorizer::opa::OpaAuthorizer::new`]. Defaults
are picked to match Strimzi's `KafkaAuthorizationOpa` (`50_000` LRU
entries, 1 h TTL, fail-closed on OPA error).

allow_on_error.description:
**Security-sensitive.** Permit the operation when the OPA call
fails (timeout, 5xx, parse error). When `true`, an OPA outage
authorizes *every* request (fail-open). Default `false`
(fail-closed) — omitting this field denies on error, matching the
upstream Open Policy Agent Kafka plugin's `allow.on.error = false`.

expire_after_ms.description: Decision TTL, in milliseconds. Default `3_600_000` (1 h).

maximum_cache_size.description: LRU cache capacity, in entries. Default `50_000`.

url.description:
OPA decision endpoint URL — must include the data-API path,
e.g. `http://opa:8181/v1/data/kafka/authz/allow`.

FileOperatorKey.description:
TOML shape of one `[[operator_keys]]` entry. Maps to
[`crate::operator_keys::OperatorKeyEntry`].

`deny_unknown_fields` so a misspelled key is rejected at parse time. An
ignored `principal` typo would leave a key bound to nobody, and the
principal binding is what stops one operator's key signing in another
operator's name.

key_id.description:
Stable identifier that a signed freeze record or break-glass approval
names. Must be unique across the array.

principal.description:
The principal this key speaks for, e.g. `"User:alice"`. Must be unique
across the array. The broker refuses a signed record whose claimed
author is not this principal.

public_key_path.description:
Path to the raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key, the bytes an
[`krabka_audit::FileEd25519Signer`] reports as its public key. It is
read at startup, so a bad path stops the broker at boot and not in the
middle of an incident.

roles.description:
Role strings: `"controller"`, `"broker"`, `"witness"`
(case-insensitive). Empty or absent leaves the `BrokerConfig` default
`[Controller, Broker]`. A `"witness"` entry is a modifier: it must
come with both of the other two roles.

FileRemoteStorageConfig.description:
TOML shape of `[remote_storage]`. Maps to
[`crate::BrokerConfig::remote_storage_backend`].

Exactly one of `storage_dir` (local filesystem), `[remote_storage.s3]`
(S3-compatible object store), or `[remote_storage.gcs]` (native Google
Cloud Storage) should be set. Setting more than one errors at load time.

copier_threads.description:
How many partitions may be copying segments to the remote tier at
once. Kafka's `remote.log.manager.copier.thread.pool.size`; defaults
to 10. Raising it is the remedy for a copy backlog on an object store
with bandwidth to spare.

copy_timeout.description:
Deadline on one segment copy to the remote tier. Defaults to 10
minutes.

A partition holds one copier slot for the whole of its copy pass, so a
copy that hangs on a stalled object store spends that slot on a
partition moving no bytes. Past this deadline the copy is abandoned
and retried on the next tick; the segment stays in
`CopySegmentStarted`, which local retention refuses to delete
against.

expiration_threads.description:
How many partitions may be running their local- and remote-retention
passes at once. Kafka's
`remote.log.manager.expiration.thread.pool.size`; defaults to 10.

gcs.description:
Native Google Cloud Storage backend parameters. Omit to use
`storage_dir` or `[remote_storage.s3]`.

index_cache_size.description:
Byte budget of the on-disk cache of remote segment indexes under
`<log_dir>/remote-log-index-cache`. Kafka's
`remote.log.index.file.cache.total.size.bytes`; defaults to 1 GiB.

kafka_metadata.description:
Opt-in to the topic-backed `RemoteLogMetadataManager`.
When absent, the broker uses the in-memory fixture.

reader_max_pending_tasks.description:
How many cold-tier reads may wait for a reader slot before one is
refused. Kafka's `remote.log.reader.max.pending.tasks`; defaults to
100.

reader_threads.description:
How many cold-tier reads may run at once. Kafka's
`remote.log.reader.threads`; defaults to 10.

s3.description: S3-compatible backend parameters. Omit to use `storage_dir`.

storage_dir.description: Root directory for the local `LocalTieredStorage` backend.

worm.description:
WORM archive mode for whichever object-store backend is selected.
Presence of the table turns it on; omit it (the default) for
ordinary mutable tiered storage. Requires `[remote_storage.s3]` or
`[remote_storage.gcs]` — `storage_dir` cannot enforce write-once.

FileRemoteStorageGcsConfig.description:
TOML shape of `[remote_storage.gcs]`. Maps to
[`krabka_remote_storage::GcsConfig`].

Omitting all credential fields (`service_account_path`,
`service_account_key`, `application_credentials_path`) selects GKE
Workload Identity / Application Default Credentials (keyless) — the
primary production path.

allow_http.description:
Allow plaintext HTTP (off-by-default; required by emulators
running without TLS).

application_credentials_path.description:
Path to an Application Default Credentials JSON file. Omit (along
with the other credential fields) to use Workload Identity / ADC.

connect_timeout.description:
Ceiling on the connect phase alone. When `None`,
[`krabka_object_store::DEFAULT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`] (5s) applies.

endpoint.description: Optional custom GCS API base URL (for emulators / fakes).

max_retries.description:
How many times one object-store request is retried before the error
reaches the broker. When `None`, [`krabka_object_store::DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES`]
(10) applies; `0` disables retries. Under a store that answers
`503 SlowDown` this is what bounds how long one call holds its
caller before the failure is counted and the sweep moves on.

multipart_chunk_size.description:
Optional override of the per-part multipart chunk size (bytes).
When `None`, [`krabka_remote_storage::DEFAULT_MULTIPART_CHUNK_SIZE`]
applies.

multipart_threshold.description:
Optional override of the multipart-upload threshold (bytes). When
`None`, [`krabka_remote_storage::DEFAULT_MULTIPART_THRESHOLD`]
applies. Operators typically leave this alone; lower it to force
multipart on smaller segments for testing.

prefix.description:
Optional key prefix inside the bucket (lets multiple clusters
share a bucket).

request_timeout.description:
Ceiling on one HTTP request, connect phase included. When `None`,
[`krabka_object_store::DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`] (30s) applies. This
is the bound on a store that accepts the connection and then
answers nothing.

retry_timeout.description:
Ceiling on the wall-clock time one request may spend across all of
its retries. When `None`,
[`krabka_object_store::DEFAULT_RETRY_TIMEOUT`] (3m) applies. Keep it
under 5 minutes: retries reuse the original request's credentials.

service_account_key.description:
Inline service-account JSON key. Omit (along with the other
credential fields) to use Workload Identity / ADC.

service_account_path.description:
Path to a service-account JSON key file. Omit (along with the
other credential fields) to use Workload Identity / ADC.

access_key_id.description:
Explicit access key id. Falls back to the AWS credential chain
(env vars, instance profile, …) when omitted.

allow_http.description:
Allow plaintext HTTP (off-by-default; required by `MinIO` running
without TLS).

checksum_sha256.description:
Optional override of the `x-amz-checksum-sha256` header, which has the
server verify each object on ingest. When `None`, the
[`krabka_remote_storage::S3Config`] default of `true` applies.

conditional_put.description:
Optional override of conditional puts (`If-None-Match`), which make a
create-mode write fail on an existing key instead of overwriting it.
When `None`, the [`krabka_remote_storage::S3Config`] default of `true`
applies. Turn it off only for an S3-compatible store that mishandles
the header; WORM archive mode relies on it.

connect_timeout.description:
Ceiling on the connect phase alone. When `None`,
[`krabka_object_store::DEFAULT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`] (5s) applies.

endpoint.description: Optional custom endpoint URL (e.g. `MinIO` or Cloudflare R2).

max_retries.description:
How many times one object-store request is retried before the error
reaches the broker. When `None`, [`krabka_object_store::DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES`]
(10) applies; `0` disables retries. Under a store that answers
`503 SlowDown` this is what bounds how long one call holds its
caller before the failure is counted and the sweep moves on.

multipart_chunk_size.description:
Optional override of the per-part multipart chunk size (bytes).
When `None`, [`krabka_remote_storage::DEFAULT_MULTIPART_CHUNK_SIZE`]
applies. AWS requires parts ≥ 5 MiB except the last; `MinIO`
tolerates smaller values.

multipart_threshold.description:
Optional override of the multipart-upload threshold (bytes). When
`None`, [`krabka_remote_storage::DEFAULT_MULTIPART_THRESHOLD`]
applies. Operators typically leave this alone; lower it to force
multipart on smaller segments for testing.

prefix.description:
Optional key prefix inside the bucket (lets multiple clusters
share a bucket).

region.description: AWS region. Required even for non-AWS endpoints (use any value).

request_timeout.description:
Ceiling on one HTTP request, connect phase included. When `None`,
[`krabka_object_store::DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`] (30s) applies. This
is the bound on a store that accepts the connection and then
answers nothing.

retry_timeout.description:
Ceiling on the wall-clock time one request may spend across all of
its retries. When `None`,
[`krabka_object_store::DEFAULT_RETRY_TIMEOUT`] (3m) applies. Keep it
under 5 minutes: retries reuse the original request's credentials.

secret_access_key.description:
Explicit secret access key. Falls back to the AWS credential chain
when omitted.

credentials_path.description:
Filesystem path to the SASL/PLAIN credential file: one
`username=password` per line, split at the first `=`, so a password may
contain `=`. Line endings are stripped. A line whose trimmed content is
empty or starts with `#` is ignored. The username is trimmed of
surrounding whitespace, since it is matched against the SASL authcid
and padding there is a typo rather than intent; the password is stored
exactly as written, including any leading or trailing whitespace, so a
secret is never silently rewritten. File-based (not literal) so no
password sits in the TOML; the operator mounts a `Secret` and writes
the mount path here.

FileSchemaRegistryConfig.description:
TOML shape of `[schema_registry]`. Mirrors the constructor arguments of
[`crate::schema_validation::SchemaValidator::new`], the one registry client
each broker holds.

`deny_unknown_fields` so a misspelled key is rejected at parse time. A
silently ignored `fail_open` would leave the operator with the opposite of
the policy they wrote.

basic_auth_password_path.description:
File containing the HTTP Basic password. One trailing newline is ignored.

Set this together with `basic_auth_username`; keeping the password in a
separate mounted secret avoids putting it in broker arguments or TOML.

basic_auth_username.description:
HTTP Basic username for an authenticated registry.

Set this together with `basic_auth_password_path`.

expire_after_ms.description:
Schema-cache entry TTL, in milliseconds. Default `300_000`, which is
5 minutes.

fail_open.description:
**Security-sensitive.** Admit a record that the broker could not
validate because the registry was unreachable. When `true`, a validated
topic accepts whatever it is sent for the length of a registry outage.
That is fail-open. Default `false`, which fails the produce instead.

An unknown schema id, or a body that does not match its schema, is a
rejection under either setting. This field governs only the case where
the broker could not get an answer at all.

url.description:
Base URL of the Confluent-compatible schema registry, e.g.
`http://schema-registry:8081`. The registry API path is appended to it.

FileStretchConfig.description:
`[stretch]` TOML section — the three-site stretch deployment.

The table is all-or-nothing. When it is present, all three fields must
be, because a half-built profile would let the broker start with a site
layout that no node agrees on.

preferred_leader_site.description:
The site that partition leadership prefers while both data sites are
up. It must not be the witness site.

sites.description:
The three site names. Each one is a `rack` value that some node of
the cluster reports.

witness_site.description: The site that holds the witness nodes.

cert_path.description: PEM file holding this listener's server certificate chain.

client_auth.description:
Whether this listener asks for and requires a client certificate.
See [`FileClientAuthMode`]. Defaults to `Disabled`.

client_ca_path.description:
PEM file of CA(s) this listener validates client certificates
against. Absent leaves mTLS without a client trust store, so
`client_auth` has to be `Disabled`.

key_path.description: PEM file holding the private key for `cert_path`.

principal_mapping_rules.description:
KIP-371 `ssl.principal.mapping.rules`: how the Subject DN of an mTLS
peer certificate becomes the principal name ACLs and `super_users` are
written against. Each entry is either `DEFAULT`, which uses the DN
itself, or `RULE:pattern/replacement/[L|U]`, where `pattern` has to
match the whole DN, `replacement` may reference capture groups as `$1`,
and a trailing `L` or `U` lowercases or uppercases the result. The
rules are tried in order and the first match wins. Defaults to
`["DEFAULT"]`, so a listener that says nothing keeps Kafka's behaviour
of using the full DN. A malformed entry is rejected at startup.
Case-insensitive backreferences have a Unicode compatibility edge:
under `(?i)`, non-ASCII case pairs may match here when Java rejects
them (for example `é` and `É`); under `(?iu)`, pairs Java accepts may
fail here (for example `i` and `İ`, or `s` and `ſ`). Ordinary ASCII
DNs are unaffected. Keep both captured and referenced text ASCII, or
avoid case-insensitive backreferences when exact Java behavior matters.

trust_roots_path.description:
PEM file of CA(s) this broker trusts when validating a PEER's server
cert as an outbound inter-broker / controller-quorum dialer. The
operator renders the cluster CA here so KIP-595 controller peers can
mutually authenticate over the controller listener. Maps to
[`krabka_security::TlsConfig::trust_roots_path`].

FileTopicPolicyConfig.description:
TOML shape of `[topic_policy]`. Maps to
[`crate::topic_policy::TopicPolicy`].

The whole table is the KIP-108 / KIP-133 policy Kafka loads from a Java
class named by `create.topic.policy.class.name` and
`alter.config.policy.class.name`. krabka cannot load a class, so the rules
are declared here instead. Omitting the table declares no rule, which is
Kafka's default of no policy class: every `CreateTopics` and every topic
`AlterConfigs` that passes ordinary config validation is accepted.

A request that breaks a rule is answered with `POLICY_VIOLATION` (44) and
an `error_message` naming the rule, which is what a `PolicyViolationException`
from a Java policy class produces. The two replica rules apply to
`CreateTopics` alone, because an `AlterConfigs` request carries neither
number, exactly as `AlterConfigPolicy.RequestMetadata` does not.

`deny_unknown_fields` so a misspelled rule name is rejected at parse time
rather than leaving the broker enforcing nothing where the operator wrote
a rule.

forbidden.description:
Config keys the topic must not set to the named value, written as a
TOML table:
`forbidden = { "unclean.leader.election.enable" = "true" }`. Any other
value for that key, and omitting the key, both pass.

max_partitions.description:
Highest partition count `CreateTopics` may be asked for, checked
against the effective count. Omitted enforces no ceiling. Must be at
least 1.

min_insync_replicas.description:
Lowest `min.insync.replicas` a topic may carry. A topic that does not
set the key passes: it runs on the cluster default, which the same
operator sets. Omitted enforces no floor. Must be at least 1.

min_replication_factor.description:
Lowest replication factor `CreateTopics` may be asked for. The
effective factor is checked, so a request that leaves it `-1` is
judged on the factor the placement resolved. Omitted enforces no
floor. Must be at least 1.

required.description:
Config keys the topic must set, with the exact value it must set them
to, written as a TOML table:
`required = { "cleanup.policy" = "delete" }`. A topic that omits the
key, or sets it to another value, is refused.

FileWormConfig.description:
TOML shape of `[remote_storage.worm]`. Maps to
[`krabka_remote_storage::WormConfig`]. Presence of the table enables WORM
archive mode.

Unlike [`FileRemoteStorageS3Config`] this derives `Debug` plainly, and that
is deliberate: it holds a *path* to a signing key and the key's public id,
neither of which is credential material, and an operator debugging a chain
needs to see which key signed it. Do not "fix" this into a redacting impl.

signing_key_id.description:
Stable identifier recorded in every manifest signature, so a chain
stays verifiable across a key rotation.

Default: unset. Setting this requires `signing_key_path` as well.

signing_key_path.description:
Path to the `PKCS#8` Ed25519 key that signs each segment manifest.

Default: unset. Manifests then carry no signature, and the archive
keeps only the per-object digests and the hash chain. Setting this
requires `signing_key_id` as well.

write_only.description:
Refuse every remote fetch from this archive.

Default: `false`. When `true`, remote fetch is unavailable: a consumer
that asks for an offset whose local segment has already been evicted
gets an error, not a slow read. The archive is then a compliance sink,
not a storage tier.

audit_event_queue_capacity.description: Capacity of the asynchronous audit event queue.

audit_partition_wait_timeout.description: Maximum wait for the audit partition to become available.

audit_spool_replay_interval.description: Cadence at which the audit spool replays records it could not append.

audit_stats_poll_interval.description: Cadence of the audit statistics poll.

audit_tail_read_max.description: Maximum bytes read by one audit tail request.

audit_tail_window_offsets.description: Number of offsets included in one audit tail request.

auto_join_retry_backoff.description: Retry delay between KIP-853 dynamic-quorum auto-join attempts.

auto_join_voter_request_timeout.description: Timeout carried by a dynamic-quorum `AddRaftVoter` request.

barrier_injection_timeout.description: Deadline for one barrier injection to reach every target partition.

barrier_max_groups.description: Maximum number of barrier groups the cluster accepts.

barrier_max_topics_per_group.description: Maximum number of topics in one barrier group.

barrier_min_injection_interval.description: Shortest periodic injection interval a barrier group may ask for.

barrier_recovery_read_max.description: Maximum bytes requested by one `__barrier_state` recovery read.

barrier_retained_cuts.description: Number of cuts a barrier group keeps before it tombstones the oldest.

barrier_state_num_partitions.description: Partition count of the `__barrier_state` internal topic.

barrier_state_replication_factor.description: Replication factor of the `__barrier_state` internal topic.

classic_group_initial_rebalance_delay.description:
Initial delay before a classic group begins rebalancing, Kafka's
`group.initial.rebalance.delay.ms`. Zero completes a new group's first
rebalance as soon as its first member joins.

classic_group_max_session_timeout.description:
Upper bound on a classic `JoinGroup` session timeout, Kafka's
`group.max.session.timeout.ms`.

classic_group_max_size.description:
Maximum number of members in one classic group, Kafka's
`group.max.size`.

classic_group_min_session_timeout.description:
Lower bound on a classic `JoinGroup` session timeout, Kafka's
`group.min.session.timeout.ms`.

client_metrics_default_interval.description: Default KIP-714 client telemetry subscription push interval.

client_metrics_enable.description:
Whether the broker advertises the KIP-714 client-metrics RPCs,
`GetTelemetrySubscriptions` (71) and `PushTelemetry` (72). Kafka
advertises them only when `metric.reporters` holds a `ClientTelemetry`
implementation, so the default here is `false` as well and a client
starts no telemetry handshake the broker has nowhere to forward. A
configured `[telemetry]` OTLP endpoint turns them on without this key.

client_metrics_eviction_tick.description: Cadence at which the KIP-714 client-metrics cache evicts entries.

client_metrics_otlp_queue_capacity.description: Capacity of the client-metrics OTLP forwarding queue.

client_metrics_prom_snapshot_ttl.description: Lifetime of a Prometheus client-metrics snapshot.

client_metrics_stale_floor.description: Minimum age at which a client-metrics entry counts as stale.

client_metrics_stale_push_intervals.description: Number of missed push intervals after which client metrics expire.

client_metrics_telemetry_max.description: Maximum accepted KIP-714 client telemetry payload size.

connection_failed_authentication_delay.description:
How long a failed SASL authentication holds its response and the close
that follows, Kafka's `connection.failed.authentication.delay.ms`. Zero
closes at once.

consumer_group_heartbeat_interval.description:
Default KIP-848 consumer-group heartbeat interval, Kafka's
`group.consumer.heartbeat.interval.ms`.

consumer_group_max_heartbeat_interval.description:
Upper bound on the negotiated consumer-group heartbeat interval,
Kafka's `group.consumer.max.heartbeat.interval.ms`.

consumer_group_max_session_timeout.description:
Upper bound on the negotiated consumer-group session timeout, Kafka's
`group.consumer.max.session.timeout.ms`.

consumer_group_max_size.description:
Maximum number of members in one consumer group, Kafka's
`group.consumer.max.size`.

consumer_group_min_heartbeat_interval.description:
Lower bound on the negotiated consumer-group heartbeat interval,
Kafka's `group.consumer.min.heartbeat.interval.ms`.

consumer_group_min_session_timeout.description:
Lower bound on the negotiated consumer-group session timeout, Kafka's
`group.consumer.min.session.timeout.ms`.

consumer_group_session_timeout.description:
Default KIP-848 consumer-group session timeout, Kafka's
`group.consumer.session.timeout.ms`.

controlled_shutdown_drain_timeout.description:
How long a controlled shutdown waits for the controller to acknowledge
`should_shut_down` before it falls back to a hard shutdown.

controller_election_timeout.description:
Controller election timeout, Kafka's
`controller.quorum.fetch.timeout.ms`. It is the follower fetch
watchdog, and 1.5x of it is the leader's check-quorum window: a leader
that a majority of the voters has not fetched from within that window
resigns its epoch.

controller_fetch_miss_limit.description: Consecutive follower fetch misses tolerated before a new election.

controller_heartbeat_interval.description:
Raft heartbeat interval on the controller quorum. It should stay at or
below `controller_election_timeout / 3`.

controller_mutation_quota_window.description:
Time window whose throughput defines the KIP-599 controller-mutation
quota burst capacity (default 11 s), Kafka's
`controller.quota.window.num` x `controller.quota.window.size.seconds`.

coordinator_actor_mailbox_capacity.description: Mailbox capacity of each coordinator actor.

coordinator_session_expiry_tick.description: Cadence of the consumer-group session expiry scan.

coordinator_shutdown_ack_timeout.description: Maximum wait for coordinator shutdown acknowledgements.

dedup_max_entries.description:
Maximum number of KFC-10 dedup index entries that all partition
replicas on this broker hold together. An entry takes about 64 B, so
the default of 16000000 takes about 1 GiB of memory. The partitions
share this budget, and a partition that inserts while the broker is
near the limit trims its own index. The broker reads it at startup. The
value must be at least 1.

dedup_max_entries_per_partition.description:
Maximum number of KFC-10 dedup index entries, one for each distinct
identity, that one partition replica holds. At the limit the index
trims its oldest entries. If it can free none, it admits new identities
without indexing them. The broker reads it at startup. The default is
1000000, and the value must be within 1..=10000000.

default_min_insync_replicas.description:
Broker default for a topic's `min.insync.replicas`, Kafka's
`min.insync.replicas`. A topic override wins over it.

default_replication_factor.description:
Replication factor of a topic that `CreateTopics` creates with
`replication_factor = -1`, Kafka's `default.replication.factor`.

delegation_token_default_renew_period.description:
KIP-48: default renew period, Kafka's
`delegation.token.expiry.time.ms`. It is the initial expiry offset at
create time, and the implicit renew period when a
`RenewDelegationToken` request asks for `-1`.

delegation_token_expiry_check_interval.description:
KIP-48: cadence of the sweep that tombstones expired delegation tokens,
Kafka's `delegation.token.expiry.check.interval.ms`.

delegation_token_max_lifetime.description:
KIP-48: hard upper bound on a delegation token's lifetime, Kafka's
`delegation.token.max.lifetime.ms`. A renew request is clamped to it.

diskless_wal_flush_interval.description: Cadence of diskless WAL flushes to the object store.

diskless_wal_flush_max_size.description: Maximum bytes included in one diskless WAL object-store flush.

diskless_wal_hot_tail_max_size.description:
Broker-wide byte ceiling for quorum-committed diskless hot-tail
batches.

diskless_wal_index_projection_timeout.description: Maximum wait for a published diskless WAL index record to be projected.

diskless_wal_local_replica_count.description: Local replica count used in diskless WAL mode.

diskless_wal_trim_safety_lag.description: Committed offsets retained behind the diskless WAL trim frontier.

fetch_max_bytes.description:
Maximum bytes returned by one consumer `Fetch` or `ShareFetch`,
Kafka's `fetch.max.bytes`. Kafka's default is 57,671,680 bytes.

future_log_move_read_chunk.description: Bytes copied per read during a KIP-113 future-log move.

future_log_move_retry_backoff.description: Retry delay after a KIP-113 future-log move fails.

gauge_poll_interval.description: Cadence at which broker gauges are refreshed.

heartbeat_interval.description: How often this broker sends `BrokerHeartbeat` to the controller leader.

heartbeat_timeout.description:
How long the controller waits without a heartbeat before it marks a
broker dead.

inter_broker_server_name.description:
TLS SNI and SASL server name used for outbound inter-broker
connections.

leader_imbalance_check_interval.description:
How often the auto-rebalance ticker fires, Kafka's
`leader.imbalance.check.interval.seconds`.

legacy_request_versions_enable.description:
Whether the broker serves the request versions Kafka 4.x removed:
`Fetch` v0-v3, `ListOffsets` v0 and `Produce` v0-v2. krabka-only, with
no Kafka equivalent. The default is `false`, which advertises and
accepts exactly Kafka 4.3.1's minimums (`Fetch` v4, `ListOffsets` v1,
and `Produce` v3 though it is still advertised from v0, KAFKA-18659)
and closes a connection that sends an older version, as a 4.3.1 broker
does. `true` keeps a pre-0.11 client working.

log_delivery_clock_uncertainty.description:
Declared bound on how far this broker's clock can be from true time. It
has an effect only under the scheduled delivery policy: a batch becomes
visible once `max_timestamp + log_delivery_clock_uncertainty <= now`,
so delivery is never early and is late by at most twice this bound.

log_read_ahead_max.description:
Cap on how far past a fetch read's own byte range the broker asks the
kernel to read ahead, so a consumer that is behind finds its next fetch
in the page cache. The hint reaches up to one more range of the same
size, and no further than this. The default is 4 MiB, and 0 limits the
hint to the fetch's own range. The hint has no effect on a host other
than Linux.

log_read_buffer_cap.description: Cap on the initial allocation a decoded or raw segment read makes.

log_retention_check_interval.description:
Cadence of local-retention maintenance: how often `retention.ms`,
`retention.bytes` and `segment.ms` are applied to every hosted log.

log_segment_bytes.description:
Roll the active segment once it grows past this. Kafka's
`log.segment.bytes`, the broker default for a topic's `segment.bytes`.

log_tail_cache_size.description:
How much of the newest data a partition with `preallocate=true` keeps
in memory to serve reads with. Such a partition writes its active
segment through `O_DIRECT`, which bypasses the page cache, so without
this a consumer reading right behind the producer reads from disk.
Every such partition holds up to this much, plus one batch. The
default is 1 MiB, and 0 keeps only the newest batch.

log_timestamp_scan_window.description: Size of the window a timestamp search reads the log in.

max_connections.description:
Maximum number of live broker connections across all listeners, Kafka's
`max.connections`. A connection accepted past this ceiling is closed
immediately.

max_connections_per_ip.description:
Maximum number of live connections from any single client IP, Kafka's
`max.connections.per.ip`.

max_incremental_fetch_session_cache_slot.description:
KIP-227: maximum number of incremental-fetch sessions kept in the per-
broker cache, Kafka's `max.incremental.fetch.session.cache.slots`. When
the cache is full, a new session displaces only a session that has been
unused for more than two minutes, or a smaller one created more than two
minutes ago (a follower-fetch session may also displace any consumer
session); otherwise it is refused and the fetch runs sessionless, as in
Kafka's `FetchSessionCacheShard.tryEvict`.

max_produce_group.description: Maximum number of produce requests combined into one append group.

message_max_bytes.description:
Kafka's broker-wide `message.max.bytes`: the largest record batch a
topic that sets no `max.message.bytes` accepts.

metadata_log_segment_bytes.description:
Largest size of one metadata-log segment, Kafka's
`metadata.log.segment.bytes`. The active segment rolls before an
append that takes it past this size. A whole number of bytes from
8 MiB to 2147483647 bytes, as Kafka's `INT` with `atLeast(8388608)`.

metadata_log_segment_roll_interval.description:
Longest time one metadata-log segment stays active, Kafka's
`metadata.log.segment.ms`. A positive whole number of milliseconds.

metadata_max_bytes_between_snapshots.description:
Committed metadata-log bytes between snapshots, Kafka's
`metadata.log.max.record.bytes.between.snapshots`.

metadata_max_idle_interval.description:
KIP-835: how often the active controller appends a `NoOpRecord` to the
metadata log, Kafka's `metadata.max.idle.interval.ms`. A whole number
of milliseconds up to 2147483647 ms. Zero disables the no-op records.

metadata_max_retention.description:
Age after which a metadata snapshot and the log prefix it covers are
deleted, Kafka's `metadata.max.retention.ms`. A whole number of
milliseconds. Zero is a value. Kafka's negative value, which sets no
age limit, has no form here.

metadata_max_retention_bytes.description:
Largest combined size of the metadata log and its snapshots before the
oldest snapshot and the log prefix it covers are deleted, Kafka's
`metadata.max.retention.bytes`. A whole number of bytes. Zero is a
value. Kafka's negative value, which sets no size limit, has no form
here.

metadata_max_snapshot_interval.description:
Maximum time between metadata-log snapshots, Kafka's
`metadata.log.max.snapshot.interval.ms`. Zero disables the time-based
cap.

metadata_raft_command_queue_capacity.description: Capacity of the metadata Raft engine command queue.

metadata_raft_fetch_max.description: Per-read and per-snapshot-request byte budget on the metadata Raft log.

metadata_snapshot_fetch_max.description:
Maximum metadata snapshot size a follower fetches. The Raft core
enforces an immutable 1 GiB ceiling above it.

metadata_snapshot_interval_records.description:
KIP-630: snapshot the metadata log once the committed offset advances
this many records past the last snapshot. The metadata log keeps the
records below a snapshot until its retention limits let them go.

num_partitions.description:
Partition count of a topic that `CreateTopics` creates with
`num_partitions = -1`, Kafka's `num.partitions`.

oauth_jwks_http_timeout.description: Timeout for one OAuth JWKS fetch.

observer_fetch_max.description: Maximum bytes fetched by one metadata observer request.

observer_lag_bound.description:
KIP-853: maximum log-entry lag an observer may have and still be
promotable to a voter.

observer_poll_interval.description: Cadence of the KIP-853 observer promotion poll.

offsets_retention.description:
How long a committed consumer offset is kept after its group becomes
empty, Kafka's `offsets.retention.minutes`. It must be a whole number
of minutes.

offsets_retention_check_interval.description:
Cadence of the expired-offset sweep, Kafka's
`offsets.retention.check.interval.ms`.

offsets_topic_num_partitions.description:
Partition count of the `__consumer_offsets` internal topic, Kafka's
`offsets.topic.num.partitions`.

offsets_topic_replication_factor.description:
Replication factor of the `__consumer_offsets` internal topic, Kafka's
`offsets.topic.replication.factor`.

opa_http_timeout.description: Timeout for one OPA authorization request.

operator_recovery_deadline.description: Deadline for an operator-triggered unclean recovery.

partition_disk_scan_interval.description:
Cadence of the partition disk-usage scan that feeds the
`partition_disk_bytes` gauge. Zero disables the scanner and spawns no
background task.

partition_writer_queue_depth.description: Capacity of each partition-writer request queue.

producer_id_expiration.description:
How long a producer id may stay idle before its state expires, Kafka's
`producer.id.expiration.ms`.

producer_id_expiration_scan_interval.description:
Cadence of the producer-state expiry scan, Kafka's
`producer.id.expiration.check.interval.ms`.

queued_max_request_bytes.description:
Maximum byte size across all queued requests before accepting
additional requests is paused, Kafka's `queued.max.request.bytes`.

queued_max_requests.description:
Maximum number of queued requests allowed in the broker dispatch queue,
Kafka's `queued.max.requests`.

quota_throttle_max.description:
Maximum request-quota throttle delay, which bounds how long one
response over `request_percentage` mutes a client. Equivalent to
Kafka's `quota.window.size.seconds`; byte-rate and controller-mutation
throttles are not bounded.

quota_window.description:
Time window that sizes the client byte-rate quota token bucket's burst
capacity. Equivalent to Kafka's sampling window `quota.window.num *
quota.window.size.seconds`.

record_decompression_max_ratio.description: Maximum accepted decompression ratio for a produced record batch.

record_decompression_output_ceiling.description: Maximum decompressed-output allowance granted to a record batch.

record_decompression_output_floor.description:
Minimum decompressed-output allowance granted to a record batch,
whatever the ratio bound computes.

remote_log_manager_interval.description:
KIP-405: tick cadence of the `RemoteLogManager` copy and retention
task. Kafka's `remote.log.manager.task.interval.ms`.

replica_fetchers.description:
How many fetchers this broker runs per leader it follows, Kafka's
`num.replica.fetchers`. Every partition followed from one leader is
hashed onto one of that leader's fetchers, and each fetcher holds one
connection and sends one batched `Fetch` per round.

replica_lag_time_max.description:
Maximum follower lag before the leader proposes an ISR shrink. Kafka's
`replica.lag.time.max.ms`.

replication_epoch_fence_backoff.description: Retry delay after a leader-epoch fence.

replication_fetch_max.description:
Maximum bytes a follower requests from a leader in one replication
fetch. It reaches the leader as the fetch request's `max_bytes`.

replication_fetch_max_wait.description:
Maximum time a leader holds a replication fetch that is not yet
satisfied. It reaches the leader as the fetch request's `max_wait_ms`.

replication_fetch_min.description:
Minimum bytes that satisfy a replication fetch. It reaches the leader
as the fetch request's `min_bytes`, which the leader honours as a
floor.

replication_reconnect_delay_cap.description: Maximum delay between leader reconnection attempts.

replication_reconnect_initial_delay.description: Initial delay before a follower reconnects to a leader.

replication_send_error_backoff.description: Retry delay after sending a replication request fails.

replication_throttle_exhausted_backoff.description: Delay after a follower exhausts its replication throttle budget.

replication_unexpected_error_backoff.description: Retry delay after an unexpected replication error.

replication_unknown_topic_retry_delay.description: Retry delay when the leader does not yet know the topic.

rlmm_bootstrap_backoff_initial.description: Initial retry delay while remote-log metadata bootstrap is incomplete.

rlmm_bootstrap_backoff_max.description: Maximum retry delay while remote-log metadata bootstrap is incomplete.

rlmm_reconcile_tick.description: Cadence of KIP-405 remote-log metadata reconciliation.

sasl_server_max_receive.description:
Largest request frame a connection may send before it finishes
authenticating on a SASL listener, Kafka's
`sasl.server.max.receive.size`. It replaces `socket_request_max` for
that stretch, and a larger frame fails the authentication.

self_registration_backoff_max.description: Maximum delay between broker self-registration attempts.

self_registration_backoff_min.description: Initial delay between broker self-registration attempts.

self_registration_max_attempts.description: Maximum self-registration attempts before startup fails.

sendfile_min.description:
Minimum response size eligible for a `sendfile` kernel drain. Smaller
responses go through the `pread` and write copy.

share_cold_partition_snapshot_interval.description:
How old the latest snapshot of a share key may get before the share
coordinator writes a new one, Kafka's
`share.coordinator.cold.partition.snapshot.interval.ms`.

share_coordinator_append_linger_ms.description:
Kafka's `share.coordinator.append.linger.ms`, a whole number of
milliseconds, or -1 (the default) for an adaptive linger. Accepted and
has no effect: each share-state write is its own append, and the
partition writer groups concurrent appends without waiting for more.

share_coordinator_cached_buffer_max_byte.description:
Kafka's `share.coordinator.cached.buffer.max.bytes`, at least 512KiB,
default 1MiB plus 12 bytes. Accepted and has no effect: the share
coordinator encodes each record into a new buffer and keeps no buffer
for reuse.

share_coordinator_load_buffer_size.description:
Maximum bytes read by one share-state recovery read, Kafka's
`share.coordinator.load.buffer.size`.

share_coordinator_threads.description:
Kafka's `share.coordinator.threads`, at least 1. Accepted and has no
effect: the share coordinator runs as tasks on the broker's shared
async runtime rather than on a thread pool of its own.

share_coordinator_write_timeout.description:
How long an append to `__share_group_state` may take before the share
coordinator answers `COORDINATOR_NOT_AVAILABLE`, Kafka's
`share.coordinator.write.timeout.ms`.

share_group_backlog_poll_interval.description: Cadence of the share-group backlog poll.

share_group_delivery_count_limit.description:
The delivery count at which a share record is archived, Kafka's
`group.share.delivery.count.limit`: from 2 to 10, within the minimum
and maximum below.

share_group_max_delivery_count_limit.description:
Upper bound on the delivery count limit, and on a group's
`share.delivery.count.limit`, Kafka's
`group.share.max.delivery.count.limit`: from 5 to 25.

share_group_max_heartbeat_interval.description:
Upper bound on the share-group heartbeat interval, and on a group's
`share.heartbeat.interval.ms`, Kafka's
`group.share.max.heartbeat.interval.ms`.

share_group_max_partition_max_record_loc.description:
Upper bound on the record lock limit, and on a group's
`share.partition.max.record.locks`, Kafka's
`group.share.max.partition.max.record.locks`: from 2000 to 10000.

share_group_max_record_lock_duration.description:
Upper bound on the record lock duration, and on a group's
`share.record.lock.duration.ms`, Kafka's
`group.share.max.record.lock.duration.ms`: from 30s to 1h.

share_group_max_session_timeout.description:
Upper bound on the share-group session timeout, and on a group's
`share.session.timeout.ms`, Kafka's
`group.share.max.session.timeout.ms`.

share_group_max_size.description:
Maximum number of members in one share group, Kafka's
`group.share.max.size`: from 1 to 1000.

share_group_min_delivery_count_limit.description:
Lower bound on the delivery count limit, and on a group's
`share.delivery.count.limit`, Kafka's
`group.share.min.delivery.count.limit`: from 2 to 5.

share_group_min_heartbeat_interval.description:
Lower bound on the share-group heartbeat interval, and on a group's
`share.heartbeat.interval.ms`, Kafka's
`group.share.min.heartbeat.interval.ms`.

share_group_min_partition_max_record_loc.description:
Lower bound on the record lock limit, and on a group's
`share.partition.max.record.locks`, Kafka's
`group.share.min.partition.max.record.locks`: from 100 to 2000.

share_group_min_record_lock_duration.description:
Lower bound on the record lock duration, and on a group's
`share.record.lock.duration.ms`, Kafka's
`group.share.min.record.lock.duration.ms`: from 1s to 30s.

share_group_min_session_timeout.description:
Lower bound on the share-group session timeout, and on a group's
`share.session.timeout.ms`, Kafka's
`group.share.min.session.timeout.ms`.

share_group_partition_max_record_locks.description:
Maximum records a share partition may hold in flight, Kafka's
`group.share.partition.max.record.locks`: from 100 to 10000, within
the minimum and maximum below.

share_group_record_lock_duration.description:
How long an acquired share record stays locked before it is released
for redelivery, Kafka's `group.share.record.lock.duration.ms`: a whole
number of milliseconds from 1s to 1h, within the minimum and maximum
below.

share_session_cache_max_when_unlimited.description: Ceiling on the share-session cache when the group count is unlimited.

share_snapshot_update_records_per_snapsh.description:
Updates of one share key between two snapshots of it, Kafka's
`share.coordinator.snapshot.update.records.per.snapshot`. At most 500.

share_state_compression_codec.description:
Codec of the batches the share coordinator appends to
`__share_group_state`, Kafka's
`share.coordinator.state.topic.compression.codec`, as Kafka's codec
id: 0 none (the default), 1 gzip, 2 snappy, 3 lz4 or 4 zstd.

share_state_num_partitions.description:
Partition count of the `__share_group_state` internal topic, Kafka's
`share.coordinator.state.topic.num.partitions`.

share_state_prune_interval.description:
How often the share coordinator trims the redundant prefix of each
`__share_group_state` partition it leads, Kafka's
`share.coordinator.state.topic.prune.interval.ms`.

share_state_replication_factor.description:
Replication factor of the `__share_group_state` internal topic, Kafka's
`share.coordinator.state.topic.replication.factor`.

socket_request_max.description:
Maximum encoded request size accepted from a socket, Kafka's
`socket.request.max.bytes`.

startup_leader_wait_timeout.description: Maximum time the broker waits for a controller leader during startup.

streams_group_acceptable_recovery_lag.description:
Changelog lag, in records, below which a task is treated as caught up,
the group's `streams.acceptable.recovery.lag`.

streams_group_assignor.description:
Server-side task assignor for streams groups: `auto`, `sticky`, or
`highly-available`. `auto` picks `highly-available` when the topology
has a stateful subtopology and `sticky` otherwise.

streams_group_enable.description: Whether the broker serves KIP-1071 streams groups.

streams_group_heartbeat_interval.description:
Default streams-group heartbeat interval, the group's
`streams.heartbeat.interval.ms`.

streams_group_max_heartbeat_interval.description:
Highest heartbeat interval a streams group may run with, Kafka's
`group.streams.max.heartbeat.interval.ms`.

streams_group_max_session_timeout.description:
Highest session timeout a streams group may run with, Kafka's
`group.streams.max.session.timeout.ms`.

streams_group_max_size.description: Maximum number of members in one streams group.

streams_group_min_heartbeat_interval.description:
Lowest heartbeat interval a streams group may run with, Kafka's
`group.streams.min.heartbeat.interval.ms`.

streams_group_min_session_timeout.description:
Lowest session timeout a streams group may run with, Kafka's
`group.streams.min.session.timeout.ms`.

streams_group_num_standby_replicas.description:
Number of standby replicas the assignor places for each task, the
group's `streams.num.standby.replicas`.

streams_group_num_warmup_replicas.description:
Maximum number of warm-up replicas the assignor may move at once, the
group's `streams.num.warmup.replicas`.

streams_group_rack_aware_assignment_tags.description:
Client tag keys every streams-group member must send, Kafka's
`group.streams.rack.aware.assignment.tags` and the default of a
group's `streams.rack.aware.assignment.tags`. A repeated or an empty
tag key is refused.

streams_group_session_timeout.description:
Default streams-group session timeout, the group's
`streams.session.timeout.ms`.

streams_group_task_offset_interval.description:
Cadence at which members report task offsets, the group's
`streams.task.offset.interval.ms`.

sync_group_follower_wait.description:
Maximum time a classic-protocol follower waits for its `SyncGroup`
assignment.

tls_reload_interval.description:
Cadence at which the TLS watcher polls the certificate, key, and
client-CA files and rebuilds the server configuration if any changed.
Zero disables the periodic watcher.

transaction_max_timeout.description:
Maximum transaction timeout a producer may request, Kafka's
`transaction.max.timeout.ms`.

transaction_partition_verification_enabl.description:
Whether a partition leader checks with the transaction coordinator
that a transaction contains a partition before it appends
transactional records to it, Kafka's
`transaction.partition.verification.enable`. This is the static value.
A dynamic broker config of the same name, per-broker or cluster-wide,
overrides it, and the `server_properties` entry of that name applies
only when this key is absent. The default is `true`.

transaction_recovery_read_max.description: Maximum bytes requested by one `__transaction_state` recovery read.

transaction_state_num_partitions.description:
Partition count of the `__transaction_state` internal topic, Kafka's
`transaction.state.log.num.partitions`.

transaction_state_replication_factor.description:
Replication factor of the `__transaction_state` internal topic, Kafka's
`transaction.state.log.replication.factor`.

txn_abort_cleanup_interval.description:
KIP-98: how often the idle-transaction reaper scans for `Ongoing`
transactions whose timeout has elapsed and aborts them. Kafka's
`transaction.abort.timed.out.transaction.cleanup.interval.ms`. Zero
disables the reaper and spawns no background task.

txn_id_expiration.description:
KIP-98: how long a transactional id may sit in a terminal or idle state
before the coordinator tombstones it out of `__transaction_state`.
Kafka's `transactional.id.expiration.ms`.

txn_id_expiration_cleanup_interval.description:
KIP-98: how often the transactional-id expiry sweep scans the
`__transaction_state` partitions this broker leads. Kafka's
`transaction.remove.expired.transaction.cleanup.interval.ms`. Zero
disables the sweep and spawns no background task.

unclean_recovery_aggressive_deadline.description:
Replica-log collection deadline under the aggressive unclean-recovery
strategy.

unclean_recovery_balanced_deadline.description:
Replica-log collection deadline under the balanced unclean-recovery
strategy.

unclean_recovery_queue_capacity.description: Capacity of the unclean-recovery work queue.

description:
Top-level shape of `broker.toml`. `serde(deny_unknown_fields)` is
off — new fields may be added and old binaries should warn rather
than refuse to start.

audit.description:
`FedRAMP` 20x MLA audit subsystem configuration.
Absent → secure default (enabled, standard internal topic name).

authorization.description:
Pluggable cluster authorizer + super-user list.
`None` ⇒ [`crate::authorizer::AllowAllAuthorizer`] with empty
super-users (default-on-no-config behavior). When `Some`, the
`type` field selects the authorizer implementation; for
`type = "opa"`, the `[authorization.opa]` subtable is required.

bootstrap_servers.description:
KIP-853 controller discovery endpoints. Hosts remain unresolved so DNS
names can be refreshed on each retry.

break_glass.description:
`[break_glass]` section — the two-person rule over the privileged
transitions. Absent leaves the `BrokerConfig` defaults, which run no
break-glass workflow.

broker_id.description:
This node's id, Kafka's `node.id` / `broker.id`. It is the id the
broker registers with the controller and reports in `Metadata`
responses. Absent leaves the `BrokerConfig` default intact.

connections_max_idle.description:
How long a connection may go without a complete request frame before
the broker closes it (Kafka `connections.max.idle.ms`). Absent leaves
the `BrokerConfig` default of ten minutes, which is Kafka's 600000. A
`[[listeners]]` entry may carry its own `connections_max_idle`, which
wins for that listener.

connections_max_reauth.description:
KIP-368 `connections.max.reauth.ms`: how long an authenticated SASL
session may live before the client must re-authenticate in band.
Absent, or non-positive, disables re-authentication, which is Kafka's
default. It applies to every mechanism: PLAIN, SCRAM and GSSAPI
sessions are bounded by it alone, while an OAUTHBEARER or
delegation-token session expires at the earlier of its credential's
expiry and this window. A `[[listeners]]` entry may carry its own
`connections_max_reauth`, which wins for that listener.

controller_election_timeout.description:
Controller election timeout, Kafka's `controller.quorum.fetch.timeout.ms`.
It is the follower fetch watchdog, and 1.5x of it is the leader's
check-quorum window: a leader that has not been fetched from by a
majority of the voters within that window resigns its epoch. Absent
leaves the `BrokerConfig` default intact.

controller_heartbeat_interval.description: Controller heartbeat interval. Absent leaves the `BrokerConfig` default intact.

controller_listener_protocol.description:
Controller listener security protocol. When `Some(Ssl)`
the controller listener terminates TLS using `tls_config`.

controller_quorum_voters.description:
KIP-595 static controller quorum voter set. Each entry is
`<node_id>@<host>:<port>` pointing at a broker's controller listener
(port 9093). At apply time each entry is parsed (NOT DNS-resolved) and
its `<host>:<port>` is carried verbatim into
`BrokerConfig::controller_quorum_voters`. The inter-broker dialer
re-resolves the host on every (re)connect (`TcpStream::connect`), so a
peer that restarts on a new pod IP (a `StatefulSet` pod keeps its stable
DNS name but gets a fresh A record) is reached again without restarting
this broker — pre-resolving here would freeze the peer's boot-time IP
and strand a rejoining voter. Empty leaves the single self-voter the
binary seeds (standalone).

controller_server_name.description:
TLS server name (SNI) presented when dialing a PEER's controller
listener for the KIP-595 quorum. The operator renders the shared
headless-Service FQDN here — a SAN on every broker's serving cert —
so mTLS validation succeeds no matter which peer (resolved to a pod
IP) is dialed. Absent falls back to `"localhost"`. Maps to
[`crate::BrokerConfig::controller_server_name`].

delegation_token.description:
KIP-48: delegation-token master key + lifetime knobs.
Env var `KRABKA_DELEGATION_TOKEN_SECRET_KEY` wins over `secret_key`
here. When neither source provides a key, the broker disables
delegation-token auth.

extra_log_dirs.description:
Additional JBOD data directories (KIP-113). Maps to
[`crate::BrokerConfig::extra_log_dirs`].

freeze.description:
`[freeze]` section — the topic write-freeze registry's bounds and its
signature requirement. Absent leaves the `BrokerConfig` defaults.

gssapi.description:
SASL/GSSAPI (Kerberos) accept-path config. Broker-global —
there is one `[gssapi]` block per broker. Relevant when a listener
enables the `GSSAPI` mechanism.

heartbeat_interval.description:
How often this broker sends `BrokerHeartbeat` to the controller leader.
Absent leaves the `BrokerConfig` default intact.

heartbeat_timeout.description:
Controller-side session timeout for broker heartbeats. Absent leaves the
`BrokerConfig` default intact.

inter_broker_credentials.description:
Credentials this broker uses to authenticate *to* peer brokers and
controller listeners (inter-broker initiate path).

inter_broker_listener_name.description:
Name of the listener that carries inter-broker traffic — raft,
replication, and heartbeats. Kafka's `inter.broker.listener.name`. It
must match a `name` in [`listeners`][Self::listeners] when that list is
non-empty. Absent leaves the `BrokerConfig` default `"PLAINTEXT"`.

inter_broker_principal_node_ids.description:
Exact authenticated principal name to broker node ID bindings for
diskless WAL follower fetches.

log_dir.description:
Primary log directory, the first entry of Kafka's `log.dirs`. It is
the partition data directory when
[`extra_log_dirs`][Self::extra_log_dirs] is empty, and it holds the
`__cluster_metadata-0` raft log unless
[`metadata_log_dir`][Self::metadata_log_dir] names another directory.
Absent leaves the `BrokerConfig` default intact.

max_connections.description:
Maximum number of live broker connections across all listeners
(Kafka `max.connections`). Connections accepted past this ceiling
are closed immediately. Absent leaves the `BrokerConfig` default
`usize::MAX` (unlimited), matching Kafka's `Integer.MAX_VALUE`.

max_connections_per_ip.description:
Maximum number of live connections from any single client IP
(Kafka `max.connections.per.ip`). Absent leaves the `BrokerConfig`
default `usize::MAX` (unlimited).

metadata_log_dir.description:
The metadata log directory, Kafka's `metadata.log.dir`. It holds the
`__cluster_metadata-0` raft log, its snapshots, the node's
`meta.properties` and the bootstrap records. A directory that is
none of the data directories holds the metadata log only: no partition
is placed there, and `DescribeLogDirs` does not report it. Absent keeps
the metadata log in [`log_dir`][Self::log_dir], as Kafka keeps it in
the first entry of `log.dirs`. `--metadata-log-dir` wins over it.

oauthbearer.description:
SASL/OAUTHBEARER validator tuning. Only relevant when a
listener enables the `OAUTHBEARER` mechanism.

operator_keys.description:
`[[operator_keys]]` — the shared operator key trust set.

Top-level rather than nested under `[break_glass]`, because two
subsystems verify against it: a freeze record's detached signature and
a break-glass approval's. One provisioning step covers both. Empty is
the default and means no operator key is configured.

process.description:
`[process]` section — `KRaft` `process.roles`. Absent / empty leaves
the `BrokerConfig` default `[Controller, Broker]`.

rack.description: KIP-392: this broker's rack id. Maps to `BrokerConfig::rack`.

remote_storage.description:
KIP-405: tiered-storage enablement. Setting
`storage_dir` turns tiered storage on broker-wide and roots the
local reference `RemoteStorageManager` there.

replica_lag_time_max.description:
Maximum follower lag before the leader proposes ISR shrink. Absent
leaves the `BrokerConfig` default intact.

replica_selector.description:
KIP-392: replica selector name (`"leader"` | `"rack-aware"`).
Maps to `BrokerConfig::replica_selector`.

runtime.description:
Operational runtime policy. Present values replace the current broker
value; absent values retain it.

sasl_plain.description:
`[sasl_plain]` section — where the broker's static SASL/PLAIN
credential table is read from. Absent leaves the table empty, which
`BrokerConfig::validate` refuses once a listener offers PLAIN.

schema_registry.description:
`[schema_registry]` section — the Confluent-compatible registry that
supplies the schemas for KFC-7 broker-side validation. `None` means no
topic can turn schema validation on.

server_properties.description:
Raw Apache Kafka `server.properties` keys, for the settings krabka
reads under their Kafka names rather than a dedicated TOML key. The
broker consults `transaction.two.phase.commit.enable`,
`quota.window.num`, `quota.window.size.seconds`, `num.partitions`,
`default.replication.factor`, `log.roll.ms`, `delete.topic.enable`,
`auto.create.topics.enable`, `transaction.partition.verification.enable`,
the KIP-1066 `cordoned.log.dirs`, the KIP-1331
`group.streams.topology.description.plugin.class`, and Kafka's two
internal switches. krabka cannot load a JVM class, so
`group.streams.topology.description.plugin.class` accepts only
`org.apache.kafka.server.streams.InMemoryTopologyDescriptionPlugin`.
krabka builds in that plugin, which keeps the latest topology
description of each streams group in memory until the broker stops.
`unstable.api.versions.enable`
(default `false`) advertises and serves what krabka implements from
Kafka trunk beyond 4.3.1: `ApiVersions` v5 (KIP-1242),
`TxnOffsetCommit` v6 (KIP-1319), `StreamsGroupHeartbeat` and
`StreamsGroupDescribe` v1 (KIP-1331, KIP-1357),
`StreamsGroupTopologyDescriptionUpdate` (93) and `UnregisterController`
(94), `InitProducerId` v6 and with 2PC the KIP-939 `keepPreparedTxn`
recovery, and trunk's group config keys; while it is `false` every
listener serves exactly Kafka 4.3.1's API versions.
`unstable.feature.versions.enable` (default `false`) lets this node
support `metadata.version` past 4.3.1's `4.3-IV0` (30), up to trunk's
`4.5-IV0` (34), which the CIDR ACL hosts of KIP-1276 and the controller
unregistration of KIP-1312 need. Any other entry is accepted and
ignored.
A key set here loses to the equivalent dedicated key, which is applied
first.

stretch.description:
`[stretch]` section — the three-site stretch deployment this node
belongs to. Maps to `BrokerConfig::stretch`. Absent leaves the
`BrokerConfig` default `None`, an ordinary non-stretched cluster.

super_users.description:
Principals that are unconditionally authorized for
all operations, including KIP-48 delegation-token `act-as`.

Super-user status does not substitute for authentication. The
delegation-token RPCs (`CreateDelegationToken`,
`RenewDelegationToken`, `ExpireDelegationToken`) require a principal
that authenticated with SASL or mTLS, and answer
`DELEGATION_TOKEN_REQUEST_NOT_ALLOWED` (64) on a PLAINTEXT or
one-way-TLS connection whatever this list holds.

An entry may use Kafka's `User:<name>` form. As in Kafka,
`User:ANONYMOUS` is accepted: it makes every unauthenticated client a
super user, and a `PLAINTEXT` controller listener with a deny-capable
authorizer needs it.

`None` and `Some(empty)` are equivalent — both leave
`BrokerConfig.super_users` empty.

tls_config.description:
TLS material for the controller listener (and any
listener whose `protocol` is TLS-bearing).

topic_policy.description:
`[topic_policy]` section — the KIP-108 / KIP-133 rule set a topic must
satisfy before the controller commits its creation or its config
change. Absent declares no rule, which is Kafka's default of no policy
class.
